newsitem.title: IRAQ: Arbil suffers aftermath of Kurdish, Iraqi attack.
newsitem.headline: Arbil suffers aftermath of Kurdish, Iraqi attack.

text.p: Kurdish guerrillas loyal to Massoud Barzani roamed the streets of Arbil on Wednesday, as local residents struggled to cope with searing heat, no water and no electricity.
Many shops were closed but the streets were calm and there was no sign of Iraqi troops.

Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) boss for Arbil, Fadil Mirani, told reporters that his forces were in an alliance with the Iraqi army to combat aggression by Iran and treachery by Jalal Talabani, leader of the rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK).
"We were forced by the PUK and Iranian aggression. We were in circumstances 'to be or not to be'. We did not ask the Iraqi army to stay or to occupy, we did not ask for their air force," Mirani said.
Reporters went to the Kurdish parliament building -- on the southwestern edge of town. The facade of the building was holed by tank shells and showed signs of fighting.
The KDP, supported by Iraqi forces, captured the town from the PUK over the weekend.
Iraq's military incursion into the Kurdish north prompted retaliation from the United States, which on Tuesday and Wednesday launched cruise missile attacks on southern Iraq.
